explanation: Snow, full of trapped air, insulates far better than ice. Builders cut blocks from wind-packed snow and lay them in a rising spiral, so the dome holds itself up.

claims.text: Traditional domed Inuit igloos are built from blocks of packed snow, not ice.
Domed igloos are not built from blocks of solid ice, sun-dried mud or cut stone.
Snow, which holds a great deal of trapped air, insulates better than solid ice.
Igloo builders cut blocks from wind-packed snow and lay them in a rising spiral so the dome supports itself.

evidence.restatement: Snow is full of trapped air and conducts heat far less than solid ice.
Builders cut blocks from firm wind-packed snow and set them in a rising spiral that forms a self-supporting dome.

issues.note: Two distractors (Cut stone, Sun-dried mud) are implausible for an Arctic snow house, so the real choice is ice against snow. Acceptable for an easy item; more tempting alternatives would help.
